title: QA: responsive chart legend truncation + compact table row collapse + button hit-area regressions on Safari/Firefox mobile
creator: Marina Lopez
description: Summary: Running cross-browser responsive QA uncovered three correlated regressions affecting small-screen and high-density token customers: 1) Chart legend label truncation and overlap on narrow viewports (Safari iOS + Firefox Android), 2) Compact/table row collapse animation causes header misalignment and focus/scroll jump in iOS Safari, 3) Button touch-hit-area reduced after token density update, causing missed taps on Android Firefox and iOS VoiceOver awkward hit targets. Scope: ui-kit components involved: charts (Legend component), Table (compact rows + collapse/expand), Button (primary/ghost variants), and global tokens (spacing/density). Platforms: iOS Safari 17.x, iOS Safari 16.x, Firefox Android 120+, Desktop Firefox latest (responsive narrow widths). Acceptance criteria: - Chart legend wraps or collapses gracefully below 320px without overlap; labels remain readable and selectable where applicable. - Table collapse preserves header alignment during collapse/expand; no scroll jump or lost focus on iOS Safari. - Buttons maintain 44x44pt minimum touch target on mobile breakpoints (or documented deviation) and pass VoiceOver tap tests. - Accessibility: collapsed rows have correct aria-expanded/aria-controls and statically associated labels for screen readers. Known constraints: Legacy chart code uses absolute positioning for legend when width < breakpoint; Table collapse uses transform-based animation which affects layout on Safari momentum scroll. Proposed fixes: A) Charts: change legend layout to flex-wrap with a max-lines fallback; add ellipsis + tooltip for truncated labels; avoid absolute positioning on narrow widths. B) Table: swap transform animation for height/opacity transition with will-change optimizations; add a small delay to disable iOS momentum snapping during animation via -webkit-overflow-scrolling toggles; ensure ARIA attributes are set before animation starts. C) Buttons: restore token min-hit-area variable (--touch-min-size) and apply to hit-area pseudo-element; add higher z-index for stacked components to preserve tappability. Risks: Changing chart layout could affect desktop wide-layout tests; table height transition may reflow heavy tables (perf risk) — will gate behind runtime-1.18 performance review. Rollout plan: Implement fixes behind feature flags in ui-kit feature-flag:compact-collapse-fix and chart-legend-reflow; ship patch release ui-kit-2025.11.1; run focused QA on devices. Links: Design spec for responsive legend: https://drive.google.com/drive/folder/responsive-legend-spec (internal). Related engineering PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui-kit/pull/291 (WIP). Confluence triage note: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/QA-UI-Kit-Cross-Browser-Triage
steps_to_reproduce: Charts: 1) Open Dashboard demo page on iPhone 12 Safari in responsive mode. 2) Resize container to narrow width (~320px). 3) Observe legend labels overlapping or clipping into chart area. Table: 1) Open Compact table sample on iOS Safari. 2) Expand/collapse several rows in quick succession. 3) Observe header misalignment, then a scroll jump where content repositions incorrectly. Buttons: 1) View small CTA row on Android Firefox with high-density tokens (compact setting). 2) Attempt taps near button edges. 3) Observe missed taps and inconsistent visual feedback. Always reproduce on real device with network throttling off to rule out timing issues.
initial_findings: Design review (2025-11-05): confirmed charts use absolute legend container for micro-breakpoints (legacy). Engineering note (Alex Rivera, 2025-11-06): transform-based collapse was introduced to avoid layout thrash on large tables but on Safari it interacts poorly with -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch. QA (2025-11-07): button hit-area reduced after token density change introduced in tokens/density-v2 — removing the old --touch-padding value removed implicit pseudo-element used for hit expansion. Cross-team decision: prioritize table collapse fix first (high customer-impact on support queues), then buttons, then charts (charts lower severity but important for dashboards).
acceptance_criteria: - Charts: no overlap at 320px and up; labels truncated with accessible tooltips if necessary. - Table: collapse/expand animation does not cause header misalignment or scroll jumps for iOS Safari; keyboard and screen-reader focus preserved. - Buttons: minimum tappable area respected across mobile breakpoints; VoiceOver double-tap behavior unchanged. - All fixes covered by unit/regression tests and visual snapshots for desktop and mobile widths.
implementation_notes: Engineering tasks: ENG-43721 (table-collapse refactor), ENG-43722 (chart-legend responsive rewrite), ENG-43723 (button-hitarea token recovery). Design tasks: update responsive tokens spec and add visual QA checklist in Figma. QA tasks: create device matrix (iOS 15/16/17 Safari, Firefox Android 119/120, Chrome Android) and run regression harness. Flagging performance review with runtime team to validate height-transition performance on large tables. Add an e2e test that reproduces iOS fast toggle behavior using Detox or BrowserStack automation.
notes: Prefer defensive CSS and minimal JS layout adjustments; keep feature flags for staged rollout. Coordinate with Observability to track any increase in layout-shift metrics post-release.

2025-11-06 - Alex Rivera (eng): Reproduced table collapse header misalignment on iPhone 12 and iOS 16 simulator. Suspect transform: translateY is causing paint-only optimization that bypasses layout resulting in header/scroll desync. Will prototype height-based transition.
2025-11-07 - Priya Nair (PM): Prioritizing table fix P1 due to multiple customer tickets filed last week. Charts P2 but keep in same cycle for visibility. Please estimate effort by 2025-11-08.

2025-11-08 - Oliver Chen (assignee): Spike complete for table height-transition approach. Perf trade-off noted: large tables will reflow; adding will-change and requestAnimationFrame batching to mitigate. Spike notes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui-kit/issues/134 (internal).

2025-11-09 - Design review (Marina + Oliver): Decided to implement an intermediate CSS fallback: use transform for desktop, height transition for mobile breakpoints where Safari is dominant. Added aria-expanded toggles pre-animation to preserve SR announcements.

2025-11-10 - QA (Sofia Park): Began regression snapshots for compact table on BrowserStack. Found additional issue: header sticky z-index drops under floating action buttons on iOS Safari; added to bug list and linked ENG-43724.

2025-11-11 - Oliver Chen: Opened WIP PR for table collapse: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui-kit/pull/291 - includes tests and perf flags. Requesting initial design review for micro-interaction (Marina).

2025-11-12 - Marina Lopez: Reviewed PR and left comments on animation timing and accessible label propagation. Requested additional screenshot test cases for 11 different viewport widths. Also asked to include a small accessibility note for screen readers in the release changelog.
